sources.name: County flood warnings
sources.method: Collect the county feed. Check affected forecast zones and the Melbourne warning display for additional coverage.
sources.accept: Retain CAP IDs, county or reach, Actual status, issue and expiry times, replacements and cancellations. An empty successful feed describes this query at capture. A failed request leaves status unknown.

sources.name: River stage and forecasts
sources.method: Collect metadata and stageflow for GENF1 (above Lake Harney), SNFF1 (Sanford) and COCF1 (upstream at Cocoa).
sources.accept: Match station, stage units and thresholds. Record observation time, forecast issue time and each valid time. Review stale or missing series. Keep peaks labeled as forecasts until observed.

sources.name: Tributary observations
sources.method: Check gage height (00065) at the Econlockhatchee, Little Econlockhatchee, Wekiva and Lake Jesup outlet stations in the capture list.
sources.accept: Require the intended site, series, parameter and feet. Check observation age against the edition cutoff. Withhold readings older than two hours, future times and missing values. Retain qualifiers and provisional status.

sources.name: Rainfall reports
sources.method: Search Melbourne public information statements from the preceding 72 hours. Extend the window manually for an older event. Read the selected product and save its exact JSON and ID.
sources.accept: Match Seminole County, station, inches, accumulation interval, network and ending time. Record issuance separately. A missing bulletin supplies no county total.

sources.name: County notices and local access
sources.publisher: Seminole County Emergency Management and Public Works
sources.method: Read the event bulletin and local traffic viewer. Record the issuing section, location, stated as-of time and scope for roads, parks, supplies and assistance.
sources.accept: Keep standing water, closures and reopenings distinct. Confirm evacuation status with the issuing authority. If the incident page retires, mark the notice historical and find the successor through county emergency management.

sources.name: State road incidents
sources.publisher: Florida DOT / FL511 and Florida Highway Patrol
sources.method: Review the incident map, FHP listing and any FDOT advisory for the affected segment, including the county line.
sources.accept: Record route, limits, direction, agency, status and as-of time. Require explicit support for a reopening. Keep local road reports with the county source.

sources.name: Public health notices
sources.publisher: Florida Department of Health in Seminole County
sources.method: Find the dated advisory or the county bulletin attributing it to DOH-Seminole.
sources.accept: Check affected area, issue date, instructions and any withdrawal. Link the exact notice and distinguish general guidance from event-specific actions.

sources.name: Campus status
sources.publisher: Florida Department of Education and the affected institution
sources.method: Check the state storm listing and the institution's current announcement for the named campus.
sources.accept: Record the campus, effective window, reopening notice and issuer. Close an expired dated entry or mark its current status unconfirmed.

sources.name: Emergency declarations
sources.method: Trace the original signed order, amendments and extensions for each jurisdiction.
sources.accept: Record order number, signatory, county coverage and effective or expiry time. Check newer orders for changes to the covered area or dates.

sources.name: Local impact reporting
sources.publisher: Original reporting from local, state and wire outlets
sources.method: Review original reports from WFTV, Spectrum News 13, Florida public media and AP. Follow leads to the responsible agency for public instructions.
sources.accept: Record byline, publication and review times, location and original URL. Deduplicate syndicated stories. Attribute eyewitness accounts and retain each report's date.

sources.name: Reference geography
sources.publisher: Census TIGERweb, FDOT, Florida NHD and the Seminole County Water Atlas
sources.trigger: On layer, station or coverage changes
sources.method: Use the exact place, road, river, lake and boundary queries in the embedded snapshot. Check service metadata and layer IDs before rebuilding.
sources.accept: Retain CRS, retrieval date, attribution and simplification. Check community and gauge positions visually. Road geometry alone supplies no access status.

opportunities.next: Compare one SR 46 incident across FDOT and county records. Establish stable identifiers, local-road coverage and reuse terms before adding an event history.

opportunities.title: Extend rainfall coverage between bulletins
opportunities.next: Check district station coordinates, downloadable history, units and accumulation boundaries. Compare overlapping stations for one event before charting county coverage.

opportunities.next: Find a published mark in Seminole County. Verify its event, survey date, quality and vertical datum before adding a historical map point.
